$comment: A call to one of Streamlord's expression helpers as a Kotlin value written into HTML, judged by both editors alike: the author's own when its arguments are, a String otherwise, wherever it lands. A case may give `constants`, the workspace's const val names.

cases.name: a helper call with a String argument is that String: signal(q) in data-text
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun f(q: String) = elements { div { dataText("${signal(q)}") } }

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${signal(q)} into data-text, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Text from outside becomes code there, even inside quotes. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label; only a number or a boolean is safe to write in.

cases.name: a helper call with a literal argument is the author's own
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun f() = elements { div { dataText("${signal("count")}") } }

cases.name: not(q) in a script is a String

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${not(q)} into a script, which the browser runs, so escaping does not help. Put the value in a data-* attribute and read it from there.

cases.name: post(q) at the start of a URL is a String
cases.source: import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.* fun f(q: String) = "x"

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${post(q)} at the start of href, so the value decides the scheme, and a javascript: URL runs. Escaping does not help: start the value with /, # or https://, or mark the value with + in interpolate { }, which refuses a scheme that runs.
fixes: import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.* import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(q: String) = interpolate { "x" }.text

cases.name: signal(q) in the structure is a String

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${signal(q)} into the markup's own structure: a tag name, an attribute name or a list of attributes. Fine for one chosen in code; a value from outside decides the markup itself, and escaping cannot prevent that.
